papers.title: Predicting disease flares in axial spondyloarthritis using different machine learning models in the METEOR-SpA registry.
papers.abstract: To develop and externally validate machine learning models for predicting disease flares in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) using real-world registry data.
papers.summary: This study develops and externally validates machine learning models to predict disease flares in axial spondyloarthritis using real-world registry data from the METEOR-SpA cohort. The work demonstrates the feasibility of applying ML to longitudinal registry data for flare prediction, which could support proactive clinical management. External validation strengthens confidence in the models' generalizability.

papers.title: Multimodality detection of early relapse in radically treated high-risk HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: study protocol for a prospective multicentre UK cohort study (HERD).
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the seventh most common cancer globally, with over 12 000 new cases annually in the UK. Despite aggressive radical treatment, approximately 50% of patients with locally advanced (stage III/IV), human papilloma virus (HPV)-negative disease relapse within 2 years, often in the first year. Although current post-treatment follow-up schedules are recommended by clinical guidelines, imaging surveillance is led by symptoms after the initial 3 months and reliable biomarkers for early relapse are lacking. Consequently, recurrences are frequently detected
papers.summary: This paper presents a study protocol for a prospective multicentre UK cohort study (HERD) designed to detect early relapse in patients with radically treated, high-risk HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The study aims to combine multiple modalities—likely imaging, blood-based biomarkers, and clinical data—to identify recurrences earlier than current symptom-driven surveillance allows. Since about half of these patients relapse within two years, better early detection could meaningfully improve outcomes.

papers.title: PURE: An interpretable framework for prioritizing candidate regulators of differential gene expression in plants.
papers.abstract: While transcriptomic profiling has become routine, identifying the TFs underlying these expression patterns remains a major challenge, particularly for crops and non-model species lacking efficient transformation systems. To connect expression correlations with candidate regulatory mechanisms, we developed PURE (Plant Unified Regulation Explorer), an interpretable platform that ranks candidate TFs by integrating co-expression patterns with sequence motifs and experimental binding evidence. PURE uses gradient boosting to handle sparse and imbalanced plant regulatory matrices and then applies SH
papers.summary: PURE is an interpretable machine-learning platform that ranks candidate transcription factors likely to regulate differentially expressed genes in plants. It combines co-expression patterns, sequence motifs, and experimental binding evidence using gradient boosting, making it useful for crops and non-model species where experimental validation is difficult.

papers.title: Single-cell landscape reveals PLPP2 upregulation underlying radiotherapy resistance and immune microenvironment remodeling in pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this study was to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying radiotherapy resistance in pancreatic cancer by integrating single-cell transcriptomic analysis with multicenter clinical cohorts. Using machine learning algorithms and genomic data, we identified key genes associated with radiotherapy response by analyzing radiotherapy sensitivity in our center's single-cell cohort together with external multicenter cohorts, combined with immune microenvironment remodeling and metabolic reprogramming. Radiotherapy resistance- and prognosis-related genes were identified using
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell transcriptomics with multicenter clinical cohorts to uncover molecular drivers of radiotherapy resistance in pancreatic cancer. The authors identify PLPP2 upregulation as a key feature associated with resistance, alongside immune microenvironment remodeling and metabolic reprogramming. Machine learning and genomic analyses were used to pinpoint radiotherapy response genes with prognostic relevance.

papers.title: A spectral framework for measuring diversity in multiple sequence alignments.
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) methods for proteins and RNAs rely on multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) and related datasets such as experimental mutagenesis libraries, yet the amount of usable information they contain remains unclear. Here, a spectral measure of information is recast into an interpretable quantity for MSAs, denoted Leff, defined as the number of fully independent alignment positions that reproduce the observed sequence diversity. Applied to RNA MSAs, this measure shows that evolutionary constraints nearly halve diversity relative to the secondary structure alone, quantifying function
papers.summary: This paper introduces Leff, a spectral measure that quantifies the effective number of independent positions in a multiple sequence alignment by capturing how much sequence diversity is actually present. Applied to RNA alignments, it shows that evolutionary constraints reduce diversity by nearly half compared to what secondary structure alone would predict. The framework offers a principled way to assess how much usable information MSAs contain for machine learning models.

papers.title: An atlas of colonization factors in the mouse gut microbiome reveals phylogenetically structured repertoires and infection-stage-associated variation during Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice.
papers.abstract: Colonization factors (CFs) comprise CF-associated gene families related to microbial establishment, persistence, host interaction, and gut ecological fitness, but their organization and variation in the mouse gut microbiome remain poorly defined. We integrated the Mouse Gut Genome Catalogue and the Mouse Gut Protein Catalogue, clustered at 90% amino acid identity, to define CF repertoires. A total of 79 conserved CF families, comprising over 2.4 million homologs, were identified across 112,951 genomes from 2,824 microbial species. Species-level CF-associated gene profiles exhibited a clear phy
papers.summary: This study built a comprehensive atlas of colonization factor (CF) gene families in the mouse gut microbiome by integrating the Mouse Gut Genome and Protein Catalogues, identifying 79 conserved CF families across over 2.4 million homologs in 112,951 genomes from 2,824 species. The authors found that CF repertoires are phylogenetically structured and that their composition varies with infection stage during Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice.

papers.title: ProST: an image prompt-guided multimodal representation learning framework for spatial domain identification.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables gene expression profiling while preserving the spatial organization of tissues, providing a powerful tool for dissecting tissue architecture and cellular heterogeneity. However, existing methods tend to prioritize improvements in clustering performance and overlook the fundamental objective of spatial domain identification, which is the recovery of spatial regions with coherent biological structures. As a result, the generated visualizations often fail to accurately capture fine-grained tissue organization. In addition, current approaches do not fully explo
papers.summary: ProST introduces an image prompt-guided multimodal representation learning framework for spatial transcriptomics that aims to identify spatial domains reflecting coherent biological tissue structures rather than just optimizing clustering metrics. By incorporating histological image prompts, it seeks to better recover fine-grained tissue organization than existing methods.

papers.title: Self-Concentration Detection Based on Doubled Amplitude/Phase Processing in Node PDE Modular Models.
papers.abstract: Reliable classification of brain sequence cases is a challenging problem due to signal ambiguity and noise. Personal concentration is primarily determined by the base frequency of electroencephalogram (EEG) waves, i.e., the task rests on appropriate modelling and recognition of patterns in the corresponding human (in)activity (e.g., reading, relaxation, solving maths problems, etc.). Five underlying types of frequency (alpha, beta, gamma, delta, and theta) were considered as secondary input wave parameters in complex-valued node extensions to the prime amplitude in processing signals. Self-opt
papers.summary: This paper proposes a modular node-based PDE model that processes EEG signals using doubled amplitude and phase information to classify different states of personal concentration (e.g., reading, relaxation, math problem-solving). The approach leverages the five standard EEG frequency bands (alpha, beta, gamma, delta, theta) as secondary parameters within complex-valued node extensions, aiming to improve classification reliability despite signal ambiguity and noise.

papers.title: Embrace Disorder as a Function: Bio-Informed Biomaterials Design Advanced by Intrinsically Disordered Proteins.
papers.abstract: The "lock and key" model of molecular recognition, anchored by the canonical sequence-structure-function paradigm, has successfully served as a basis for designing biomimetic biomaterials for decades. This classical concept associates the function of molecules with a stable three-dimensional structure that recognizes a specific complementary surface. However, biological systems routinely achieve specificity, adaptability, and multifunctionality through protein domains that never adopt a single stable fold. Intrinsically Disordered Proteins (IDPs) and Intrinsically Disordered Regions (IDRs) rep
papers.summary: This review argues that intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and regions (IDRs), which lack stable 3D structures yet perform essential biological functions, should be embraced as design templates for biomimetic materials rather than treated as exceptions to the classic structure-function paradigm. The authors synthesize how disorder enables specificity, adaptability, and multifunctionality, and propose bio-informed strategies for engineering next-generation biomaterials inspired by these properties.

papers.title: HD-AIP: A Heterogeneous Dual-Stream Alignment-Free Framework for Anti-Inflammatory Peptide Prediction Based on Language Models and CT-Net.
papers.abstract: Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) show therapeutic potential for treating chronic and autoimmune diseases. Computational screening of these peptides remains challenging because their typically short sequences limit traditional feature extraction effectiveness, while homology-based methods incur high computational costs.
papers.summary: The authors present HD-AIP, a computational framework for predicting anti-inflammatory peptides that combines protein language model embeddings with a convolutional neural network (CT-Net) in a dual-stream, alignment-free architecture. This design avoids the high computational cost of homology-based methods and addresses the difficulty of extracting features from short peptide sequences. The tool aims to accelerate computational screening of AIPs for chronic and autoimmune disease therapeutics.

papers.title: A reference genome without a virus: cDNA reconstruction reveals the provenance and function of the MS2 phage sequence.
papers.abstract: Reference genomes are often treated as faithful representations of experimentally validated viral genomes, yet the relationship between historically curated reference sequences and infectivity is rarely tested experimentally. Here, we developed a cDNA-based reconstruction platform for the canonical RNA phage MS2 and used it to compare the current NCBI reference genome (RefSeq) with closely related published isolate sequences. We found that isolate-derived sequences reproducibly yielded infectious phage, whereas the current MS2 RefSeq-derived construct did not, showing that the present referenc
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors built a cDNA-based reverse genetics platform for the RNA phage MS2 and found that the current NCBI RefSeq reference genome does not produce infectious phage, while closely related published isolate sequences do. This shows that the curated reference sequence has diverged from a functional, infectious genome, raising concerns about treating reference genomes as experimentally validated.

papers.title: ProtThermoRank: Sequence-based multi-class prediction model for protein thermal stability changes and its application to CcsZ.
papers.abstract: Protein thermal stability is a key property of industrial enzymes and biopharmaceutical proteins. The rapid and accurate evaluation of thermal stability across large numbers of variants has become a critical step in protein engineering. However, experimental screening of large mutational landscapes remains time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. Here, we present ProtThermoRank, a sequence-based multiclass prediction model for mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability. Unlike existing approaches that encode reference and mutant sequences independently, ProtThermoRank explicitly
papers.summary: ProtThermoRank is a sequence-based multi-class model that predicts how mutations change protein thermal stability, explicitly encoding reference and mutant sequences together rather than independently. The authors apply it to CcsZ, demonstrating its utility for ranking large mutational landscapes in protein engineering without costly experimental screening.

papers.title: This must be the place: deep learning local adaptation.
papers.abstract: Climate change is increasingly disrupting the relationship between locally adapted populations and the environments in which they evolved, creating an urgent need for tools that connect genomic variation to climate. Common-garden and provenance trials remain the gold standard for characterizing local adaptation, but their time and resource requirements limit how broadly they can be applied. Genomic approaches provide a complementary path. Genotype--environment association (GEA) methods identify environmentally associated loci. Machine-learning models have also shown that geographic origin can
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a deep learning approach for detecting local adaptation from genomic data, aiming to link genetic variation to climate variables. It positions the method as a faster, more scalable complement to traditional common-garden and provenance trials, which are resource-intensive. The work falls within the broader effort to use genotype-environment association (GEA) and machine learning to predict geographic origin and environmental adaptation.

papers.title: Mapping Gene Expression to an Interpretable Semantic Space.
papers.abstract: Cell embeddings organize single-cell expression data, but their dimensions have no biological meaning, so clusters are interpreted afterward. We present MESIC (Mapping Expression to Semantic space with Interpretable Components), which builds the written knowledge about genes held in curated databases into the dimensions themselves. A biomedical language model converts each gene's summary into a semantic embedding. MESIC compresses these embeddings into a small number of components, each concentrated on a small set of genes and explained by their annotations. The components are computed once fr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MESIC is a new method that builds single-cell embeddings whose dimensions are directly interpretable by grounding them in curated gene knowledge. It uses a biomedical language model to convert gene summaries into semantic embeddings, then compresses these into a small number of components, each tied to a small set of genes and their annotations. This allows cell clusters to be interpreted through the dimensions themselves rather than only after clustering.

papers.title: VirPLM: Antigenic prediction of influenza A/H3N2 viruses with a fine-tuned protein language model.
papers.abstract: Human influenza A/H3N2 viruses undergo rapid antigenic evolution primarily driven by the hemagglutinin subunit 1 (HA1). Within HA1, amino acid substitutions under immune pressure cause antigenic drift, necessitating frequent updates to vaccine strains. While hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assays remain the gold standard for assessing antigenic relationships, their labor-intensive and low-throughput nature limits scalability. Fortunately, the rapid accumulation of HA1 sequences enables sequence-based antigenic prediction, yet effectively extracting informative representations from these viral
papers.summary: VirPLM is a fine-tuned protein language model that predicts antigenic relationships between influenza A/H3N2 viruses directly from hemagglutinin HA1 sequences, bypassing the need for labor-intensive hemagglutination inhibition assays. By learning informative representations from the rapidly growing pool of HA1 sequences, it aims to support faster, scalable vaccine strain selection.

papers.title: Regulatory-prior-guided attention preserves biological structure during unpaired single-cell RNA-ATAC integration.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing and single-cell ATAC sequencing provide complementary views of transcriptional output and chromatin regulatory potential, but integrating unpaired profiles remains challenging because the modalities differ in feature space, sparsity and noise. Existing approaches often frame integration as distribution matching, which can over-align biologically distinct, condition-specific or modality-specific cell states. We present scHPGT, a single-cell Heterogeneous Prior-Guided Transformer for regulatory-prior-guided integration of unpaired RNA and chromatin accessibility profil
papers.summary: The authors present scHPGT, a transformer-based method that uses regulatory priors (e.g., known transcription factor–target relationships) to guide integration of unpaired single-cell RNA and ATAC profiles. Unlike distribution-matching approaches that can over-align distinct cell states, scHPGT aims to preserve biological structure while aligning modalities. This offers a new strategy for multi-omic integration when paired measurements are unavailable.

papers.title: Developing SCL2205: A Protein Sequence-based Spatial Modelling Dataset for the Protein Language Model Frontier.
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) has substantially advanced protein subcellular localisation (SCL) prediction, yet its potential remains constrained by suboptimal input preparation and limited high-quality reference data. Furthermore, existing state-of-the-art (SoTA) predictors suffer from performance metric inflation due to unmitigated training-to-testing data leakage during homology augmentation. We address these challenges by introducing SCL2205, a leak-minimised benchmark dataset and pipeline curated specifically to support trustworthy, scalable, and reproducible DL-based SCL modelling.
papers.summary: The authors introduce SCL2205, a curated benchmark dataset and pipeline for predicting protein subcellular localisation that minimises data leakage between training and testing sets. They argue that existing state-of-the-art predictors report inflated performance metrics due to homology-based leakage, and SCL2205 aims to provide a trustworthy, reproducible resource for deep learning models, including protein language models.

papers.title: HERA: Bioinspired Separation of Local Fault Response and Language-Model Scheduling in Simulated Quadruped Control.
papers.abstract: Language-model inference can delay emergency supervision, but cancellation alone cannot provide an immediate physical response. HERA (Hierarchical Event-driven Reflex Architecture) separates a measurement-driven deterministic local action from language-service scheduling, with biological inspiration limited to temporal separation and local feedback. A fixed 1472-trial campaign evaluated canonical-command scheduling, simulated actuator faults and live integration. Across three workloads, the mean validated-command latency was 0.486-0.512 s with preemption, 1.476-11.101 s with single-lane FIFO a
papers.summary: HERA is a control architecture for simulated quadruped robots that separates fast, deterministic local reflex responses from slower language-model-based scheduling. In a 1472-trial evaluation, it reduced validated-command latency to roughly 0.5 seconds with preemption, compared to 1.5–11 seconds with a single-lane FIFO baseline, while still handling simulated actuator faults. The work is a bioinspired engineering demonstration rather than a biological discovery.

papers.title: 3D Spatial Interactomics Maps the Dynamics of NF-κB Multiprotein Signalosomes in Single Cells.
papers.abstract: NFκB signaling drives inflammatory responses by rapidly assembling membrane-proximal multiprotein supercomplexes, yet how these assemblies are organized in space and time within the 3D interior of a single cell has remained uncharacterized. We addressed this by profiling endogenous NFκB protein-protein interactions with an intelligent sequential proximity ligation assay (iseqPLA), read out by spinning disk confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction. Each detected protein-protein proximity event is represented by a rolling-circle amplification product, and we treat clusters of co-localized punct
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed iseqPLA, a sequential proximity ligation assay combined with 3D confocal microscopy, to map endogenous NF-κB protein-protein interactions and multiprotein signalosome assembly in single cells. This enables tracking of how NF-κB signaling complexes are spatially and temporally organized within the 3D cell interior, a previously uncharacterized aspect of the pathway.

papers.title: An open benchmark and language models for AI in aging biology.
papers.abstract: Over the past two decades, human aging has been characterized across DNA methylation, transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical modalities, yet no benchmark evaluates whether AI systems can interpret these heterogeneous data types in the context of aging biology. We introduce LongevityBench, an open suite of 17 tasks spanning five biodata domains, and use it to assess 18 frontier AI systems from six developer teams. Despite recent advances in AI, no single model dominates all tasks, with omics-based age prediction being the hardest task regardless of scale. To test whether these gaps can be clos
papers.summary: This paper introduces LongevityBench, an open benchmark of 17 tasks across five biodata domains designed to evaluate AI systems on aging biology data. Testing 18 frontier AI models reveals that no single model excels across all tasks, with omics-based age prediction proving the hardest challenge regardless of model scale. The authors also develop language models aimed at closing these performance gaps.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven decoding of maternal immune signatures in repeated pregnancy loss.
papers.abstract: Repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) is a multifactorial condition in which the underlying immunological mechanisms, particularly the disruption of maternal-fetal tolerance, remain incompletely understood. Although immune tolerance is critical for pregnancy success, the specific immune dysregulations contributing to RPL, particularly in euploid pregnancies, have been difficult to characterize. To address this, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissues from RPL patients and first-trimester controls. Our analysis initially revealed elevated expression of a transcriptional module of im
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissue from patients with repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) and first-trimester controls, combined with machine learning, to identify maternal immune signatures associated with the condition. The analysis reveals elevated expression of a transcriptional module in immune cells, providing new insights into the immunological mechanisms underlying RPL in euploid pregnancies.

papers.title: Genome-scale perturbation signatures from primary human CD4 + T cells improve genetics-based prioritization of immune drug targets.
papers.abstract: While human genetic evidence improves drug program success, target selection largely relies on associational features. Even functional features are mainly observational, capturing disease associations rather than the consequence of perturbing genes in the disease-relevant human cell type. To move beyond association, we present IGNITE (Immune Genomics and fuNctional Integration for Target Enrichment), a framework that prioritizes immune drug targets by integrating human genetic priors with features from genome-scale perturb-seq in 22 million primary human CD4 + T cells and polarized T-helper su
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present IGNITE, a framework that prioritizes immune drug targets by combining human genetic evidence with functional data from genome-scale CRISPR perturbation screens (Perturb-seq) performed in 22 million primary human CD4+ T cells and polarized T-helper subsets. By incorporating causal perturbation signatures from disease-relevant cell types rather than only observational associations, IGNITE improves the ability to identify promising immune drug targets. This demonstrates the value of large-scale functional genomics in primary human immune cells for therapeutic target discovery.

papers.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Cell Types in Describing Neuronal Physiological Features.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) captures detailed gene expression profiles at scale, while patch-clamp recordings measure intrinsic neuronal electrophysiological properties. Modeling the relations between these two modalities remains a challenge. Here, we compare how well electrophysiological features can be predicted by traditional transcriptomic cell type classification, representations derived from a foundational model (scGPT) pretrained on large-scale scRNA-seq datasets, ion channel-coding genes, and highly variable genes. Using paired transcriptomic and electrophysiological patch-s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study compares how well different transcriptomic representations predict neuronal electrophysiological features, including traditional cell type classifications, scGPT foundation model embeddings, ion channel genes, and highly variable genes. The authors find that cell type labels are surprisingly effective at describing physiological properties, often rivaling or exceeding more complex representations.

papers.title: MAPA: A Semantic Network Framework for Functional Module Discovery and Interpretation in Multi-Omics Data.
papers.abstract: Multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional molecular signatures that provide unprecedented opportunities to uncover biological mechanisms. However, translating complex molecular alterations into coherent and interpretable functional insights remains a major challenge. Existing module discovery methods can identify groups of related features, but often lack direct biological interpretability, whereas pathway-based approaches frequently yield redundant results that complicate interpretation. Here, we present MAPA (Modular Analysis and Phenotype-informed Annotation using large language mo
papers.summary: MAPA is a semantic network framework that integrates multi-omics data with large language models to discover and interpret functional modules. It addresses the interpretability gap in existing module discovery methods and the redundancy of pathway-based approaches, enabling more coherent biological insights from complex molecular signatures.

papers.title: Genolator enables protein function interpretation using a multimodal large language model fusing genomic and structural interpretation with natural language interaction.
papers.abstract: Decoding the genetic code to unveil its genome functionality is a monumental task which would greatly advance the understanding of disease mechanisms and development of targeted treatments. Although large language models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing across diverse domains, translating the complex language of DNA into human-readable form remains challenging due to genomic data complexity and unexplored regions of the human genome. Current language models either are capable of processing natural language or the genomic code. Models fusing both aspects are largely lacking.
papers.summary: Genolator is a multimodal large language model that integrates genomic sequence data with protein structural information and natural language interaction to interpret protein function. It addresses the gap where existing models handle either natural language or genomic code, but not both, enabling more accessible decoding of genome functionality for disease research and targeted treatment development.

papers.title: BAN-SDBPred: Improving Single-Stranded and Double-Stranded DNA-Binding Protein Prediction Using an Attention Network with Bilinear Convolution and Adaptive Sampling Strategy.
papers.abstract: DNA binding proteins play essential roles in numerous biological mechanisms. The DBPs can be either single-stranded binding (SSBs) or double-stranded binding (DSBs) to a DNA molecule. The in-depth identification of SSBs and DSBs has been a hot topic in bioinformatics and is involved in the drug discovery process. Traditional experimental methods failed to characterize the types of DBPs because of high cost and time constraints. While computational prediction of novel SSBs and DSBs has made significant progress, there are still challenges remaining in enhancing overall prediction performance. M
papers.summary: BAN-SDBPred is a computational tool that predicts whether a DNA-binding protein binds single-stranded or double-stranded DNA. It combines a bilinear attention network with adaptive sampling to improve prediction accuracy over prior methods. This could help prioritize proteins for drug discovery and functional studies without costly experiments.

papers.title: Deep learning radiomics based on preoperative multiparametric MRI in predicting breast cancer recurrence risk.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer treatments are often tailored to recurrence risk to improve outcomes, but reliable risk stratification methods are lacking.
papers.summary: This study applies deep learning radiomics to preoperative multiparametric MRI to predict breast cancer recurrence risk, aiming to improve risk stratification for treatment tailoring. The approach combines deep learning with radiomic feature extraction from imaging data to identify patients at higher risk of recurrence.

papers.title: miRAssist: a context-aware, evidence integration framework for interpretable miRNA-target prioritization.
papers.abstract: MicroRNA-target interaction prediction remains challenging because many existing tools provide prediction scores or ranked candidate lists without making the supporting evidence easy to interpret or relate to a specific biological context.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: miRAssist is a new computational framework that predicts microRNA-target interactions while integrating multiple lines of supporting evidence and making the reasoning behind each prediction interpretable. Unlike existing tools that output opaque scores or ranked lists, it provides context-aware, evidence-linked prioritization of candidate miRNA-target pairs. This addresses a key bottleneck in miRNA research where predictions are hard to interpret or connect to specific biological settings.

papers.title: AI-enabled multi-omics pharmacogenomic modeling guides resistance-aware multitarget optimization of venetoclax therapy in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains difficult to treat because profound molecular heterogeneity enables rapid adaptive resistance to targeted therapy. We developed an AI-driven pharmacogenomic pipeline that integrates genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, and clinical features to predict patient-specific response to venetoclax and translate resistance-associated signals into actionable therapeutic hypotheses. Across internal and external cohorts, the deep learning model showed strong discrimination and generalization (AUROC 0.84-0.90), produced calibrated probabilities, and stratified overall
papers.summary: This study develops an AI-driven pharmacogenomic pipeline that integrates genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, and clinical data to predict patient-specific responses to venetoclax in acute myeloid leukemia. The deep learning model achieved strong discrimination and generalization (AUROC 0.84-0.90) across cohorts and translated resistance-associated signals into multitarget therapeutic hypotheses. The approach aims to guide resistance-aware optimization of venetoclax-based treatment strategies.

papers.title: Computational and AI-Enabled Imaging Biomarkers for Predicting and Assessing Immunotherapy Response in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review with Functional Meta-Synthesis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Computational and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled imaging biomarkers are increasingly being investigated for immunotherapy-response assessment in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), but the evidence is heterogeneous. This systematic review identified, critically appraised, and synthesized imaging biomarkers used to predict or assess observed immunotherapy response in OSCC. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to 31 July 2026, without language restrictions. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO. Eligible studies evaluated quanti
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on computational and AI-derived imaging biomarkers for predicting or assessing immunotherapy response in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). The authors critically appraise a heterogeneous body of literature, highlighting the need for standardization and functional meta-synthesis to clarify which imaging features are most clinically useful. The work provides a consolidated reference for researchers and clinicians seeking to apply radiomics or AI-based imaging in OSCC immunotherapy.

papers.title: Explainable AI-Assisted Label-Free Raman Biosensing Reveals Therapy-Associated Spectral Signatures in Melanoma Tumors.
papers.abstract: Sensitive detection of treatment-associated Raman spectral alterations in tumor tissues remains challenging, particularly when such changes are not readily apparent from conventional morphological evaluation. Here, we developed a label-free Raman biosensing strategy combined with explainable machine learning to characterise treatment-associated spectral signatures in melanoma tumours. A B16-F10 melanoma-bearing mouse model was used to compare untreated and PBS-treated controls with cohorts receiving immune checkpoint blockade, anti-angiogenic intervention, or combination therapy. Raman spectra
papers.summary: This study combines label-free Raman spectroscopy with explainable machine learning to detect subtle spectral changes in melanoma tumors after different therapies (immune checkpoint blockade, anti-angiogenic, or combination) in a mouse model. The approach reveals treatment-associated spectral signatures that conventional morphology cannot capture, and the explainable AI component identifies which spectral features drive the classification.

papers.title: Evaluating Sequence Foundation Models for Insect Olfactory Gene Discovery: Failure Modes, Evidence Standards, and a Benchmark Agenda.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale searches for insect olfactory genes are vulnerable to rapid receptor divergence, tandem duplication, fragmented gene models, circular labels, and evolutionary leakage between training and test data. Sequence foundation models trained on DNA or proteins may extend homology-based annotation, but available evidence does not support their use as autonomous annotators or direct predictors of sensory function. This critical review organizes the problem around annotation failures rather than model catalogues. We distinguish six inference levels, from candidate locus detection to organism
papers.summary: This critical review argues that sequence foundation models are not yet reliable for autonomously annotating insect olfactory genes, citing challenges like rapid receptor divergence, tandem duplication, fragmented gene models, circular labels, and evolutionary leakage. It organizes the problem around annotation failure modes and defines six inference levels, from candidate locus detection to organism-level function, while proposing a benchmark agenda and evidence standards for future work.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Rheumatology and Systemic Inflammatory Diseases: From Pattern Recognition to Signal Analysis and Clinical Decision Support.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are transforming the landscape of rheumatological and systemic inflammatory disease management, offering unprecedented capacity to integrate complex, multidimensional data for diagnostic support, disease monitoring, and therapeutic decision-making. This comprehensive narrative review, based on a non-systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar combined with the authors' clinical expertise, provides a clinically oriented synthesis of current and emerging AI applications across the full spectrum of immune-mediated inflam
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys how AI and machine learning are being applied across rheumatology and systemic inflammatory diseases, covering diagnostic support, disease monitoring, and therapeutic decision-making. It synthesizes current and emerging applications from a non-systematic literature search, emphasizing the integration of complex multidimensional clinical data. The review is clinically oriented, aimed at helping rheumatologists understand where these tools fit into practice.

papers.title: Biological Foundation Models for Complex Disease Research and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Complex diseases, including cancer, rare genetic disorders, neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases, arise from interactions among genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states that are difficult to capture using a single data type or biological scale. Biological foundation models address this challenge by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens and learning representations that can be transferred to downstream biomedical and clinical tasks. In this review, we examine two major model classes, genomic sequence foundation models and cell foundatio
papers.summary: This review surveys biological foundation models—genomic sequence models and cell foundation models—that learn transferable representations by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens, aiming to capture the multi-scale interactions underlying complex diseases like cancer and neurodegeneration. It discusses how these models can be applied to downstream biomedical and clinical tasks, highlighting their potential for clinical translation.

papers.title: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence in Antibody Design: From Structure-Based Engineering to Generative Models.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed computational antibody engineering by enabling accurate prediction of antibody structures, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design. Recent advances in deep learning, protein language models, and generative AI have fundamentally changed the way antibodies are discovered and engineered. This review aims to present the historical evolution of computational antibody engineering, from early structure-based design strategies to modern AI-driven approaches, while highlighting the major computation
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of computational antibody engineering from early structure-based design to modern AI-driven approaches, including deep learning, protein language models, and generative AI. It highlights how these advances enable accurate antibody structure prediction, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design.

papers.title: Shared pathogenic genes and therapeutic targets in periodontitis and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis: An integrative bioinformatics and machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis (PD) and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) are chronic inflammatory diseases with potential clinical links, yet their shared molecular mechanisms remain unclear-patients with JIA face elevated periodontal risk, the temporomandibular joint affected in JIA shares inflammatory pathways with PD, Th17 cells drive both conditions, and glucocorticoid therapy may exacerbate periodontal vulnerability. This study aimed to explore the shared mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets of PD and sJIA using genetic expression data from the GEO database and performed comprehensive
papers.summary: This study integrates gene expression datasets from GEO with bioinformatics and machine learning approaches to identify shared pathogenic genes and potential therapeutic targets linking periodontitis and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis. The authors leverage the known clinical and immunological overlap between these inflammatory conditions—including shared Th17-driven pathways—to uncover common molecular mechanisms. The work highlights candidate genes that could serve as dual-purpose therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and biomarker-driven prediction of post-coronary artery bypass grafting atrial fibrillation: Integrating clinical, genomic, and metabolic insights.
papers.abstract: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) remains one of the most frequent and consequential complications after coronary artery bypass grafting, occurring in 15%-30% of patients and contributing to increased morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and higher long-term mortality. Despite decades of investigation, traditional risk models have shown limited predictive accuracy owing to the multifactorial nature of POAF.
papers.summary: This paper reviews the use of artificial intelligence and biomarker-driven approaches to predict postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting, integrating clinical, genomic, and metabolic data. It highlights that traditional risk models have limited accuracy due to the multifactorial nature of POAF, and proposes multi-omics AI integration as a path forward.

papers.title: Integrating Plant-Based Coagulation and Explainable Machine Learning for Sustainable River Water Treatment.
papers.abstract: Industrial wastewater discharge has severely degraded freshwater resources, necessitating the development of sustainable and environmentally benign treatment technologies. This study investigates the performance of three plant-based natural coagulants, namely, Moringa leaf powder (MLP), banana peel powder (BPP), and neem leaf powder (NLP), for the treatment of Sirsa River water contaminated with organic pollutants and heavy metals. Coagulation-flocculation experiments were conducted under optimized operating conditions, and treatment efficiency was evaluated based on turbidity, chemical oxygen
papers.journal: Water environment research : a research publication of the Water Environment Federation
papers.summary: This study evaluates three plant-based natural coagulants (Moringa leaf powder, banana peel powder, and neem leaf powder) for treating contaminated river water, optimizing coagulation-flocculation conditions and assessing reductions in turbidity and chemical oxygen demand. The authors also apply explainable machine learning to interpret and predict treatment performance, aiming to support sustainable, low-cost water purification.

papers.title: FatPlants 2.0: an AI-powered platform integrating plant lipid genes, pathways, and literature.
papers.abstract: Plant lipid research depends on accessible databases that connect genes, pathways, and prior literature. However, currently available resources are fragmented, species-limited, and lack AI-powered interfaces for integrated querying. FatPlants 2.0 addresses these issues by integrating ARALIP, PlantFADB, and new Cuphea/Pennycress experimental data into a unified platform with 14 000 genes/proteins, 110 pathways across 5 species, and 57 000+ curated publications. The platform features LipidBot, an AI agent enabling natural language queries via graph-based pathway search and retrieval-augmented ge
papers.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
papers.summary: FatPlants 2.0 is an updated database that unifies plant lipid gene, pathway, and literature data from multiple sources (ARALIP, PlantFADB, and new Cuphea/Pennycress data), covering 14,000 genes/proteins, 110 pathways, and 57,000+ publications across five species. It introduces LipidBot, an AI agent that lets researchers query this information using natural language, with graph-based pathway search and retrieval-augmented generation. This addresses the fragmentation and lack of AI interfaces in existing plant lipid resources.

papers.title: PhoSARte: identification of SARS-CoV-2 phosphorylation sites using contrastive learning and protein language models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation, a critical post-translational modification, is extensively altered during viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2, where it plays a central role in modulating host-pathogen interactions. Accurately identifying these specific phosphorylation sites is crucial for understanding viral pathogenesis, prioritizing antiviral targets, guiding therapeutic strategies, and strengthening preparedness for future viral outbreaks. Although several computational tools have been proposed to complement experimental phosphoproteomics, existing methods often show limited robustness, cross-viral gen
papers.summary: PhoSARte is a computational tool that combines contrastive learning with protein language models to predict phosphorylation sites specifically in SARS-CoV-2 proteins. It aims to improve on existing phosphoproteomics prediction methods, which often lack robustness and cross-viral generalization. The tool is intended to help identify host-pathogen interaction targets and prioritize antiviral drug development.

papers.title: Structure-based virulence factor classification using a dual-driven graph transformer with a pretrained language model.
papers.abstract: Bacterial pathogenicity relies on a multitude of virulence factors (VFs). Identifying these factors is crucial for comprehending the molecular mechanisms driving bacterial pathogenesis and pinpointing potential targets for antivirulence strategies. While the identification of VFs has received extensive attention, there is still a lack of prediction from the perspective of VF classes. Moreover, most computational methods focus solely on sequence information for virulence proteins, neglecting spatial structure information. Here, a novel Structure-based Dual-driven Graph Transformer framework nam
papers.summary: The authors present a structure-based deep learning framework that combines a graph transformer with a pretrained protein language model to classify bacterial virulence factors into specific functional classes. By incorporating spatial structure information alongside sequence data, the method moves beyond prior sequence-only approaches and enables class-level virulence factor prediction, which could aid in identifying targets for antivirulence strategies.

papers.title: Machine-learning in optimization of CRISPR technology.
papers.abstract: The clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-Cas system has become an indispensable tool in modern gene-engineering applications over recent years. Despite its rapid adoption, further development and broader applicability are hindered by several inherent limitations. This review surveys a range of machine-learning based approaches that aim to address these challenges. In particular, we focus on the optimization of key components of the CRISPR system, including protospacer adjacent motif recognition, Cas-protein-engineering, guide RNA sequence design and extension of t
papers.summary: This review surveys machine-learning approaches applied to optimizing CRISPR-Cas gene-editing components, including PAM recognition, Cas protein engineering, and guide RNA design. It highlights how ML can overcome inherent limitations of CRISPR systems to broaden their applicability.

papers.title: Impact of MRI modality selection on glioma sub-region segmentation using 3D U-Net and Attention U-Net: A comparative evaluation across ten MRI sequences.
papers.abstract: Accurate segmentation of glioma sub-regions is essential for treatment planning and clinical decision-making. The selection of MRI input modality plays a critical role in the performance of deep learning-based segmentation models, as each weighting captures distinct tissue contrasts and physiological characteristics. This study performed a comparative evaluation of the impact of MRI modality selection on semantic segmentation of glioma sub-regions.
papers.summary: This study compares how different MRI sequence selections affect the performance of 3D U-Net and Attention U-Net models for segmenting glioma sub-regions. Across ten MRI sequences, the authors evaluate which modality combinations yield the most accurate segmentation, highlighting that input modality choice significantly influences deep learning segmentation performance.

papers.title: PMAVP: A Mamba-Inspired Deep Learning Framework for Antiviral Peptide Identification and Functional Activity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate computational prediction of antiviral peptides (AVPs) can accelerate peptide screening and reduce experimental costs. However, existing deep learning-based methods still suffer from severe class imbalance, over-reliance on handcrafted features and limited interpretability. Here, we propose PMAVP, a multi-task learning framework that integrates the ProtT5 pre-trained protein language model with a Mamba-inspired module for AVP identification and functional activity prediction. We use ProtT5 to extract deep semantic representations from peptide sequences and a Mamba module to capture lon
papers.summary: PMAVP is a multi-task deep learning framework that combines the ProtT5 protein language model with a Mamba-inspired sequence module to identify antiviral peptides and predict their functional activity. It aims to overcome class imbalance, reliance on handcrafted features, and limited interpretability in prior methods. The approach could speed up computational screening of antiviral peptides and reduce experimental costs.

papers.title: A Hybrid and Comparative Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Gestational Diabetes Mellitus via a Prospective Case-Control Design: A Pilot Study Integrating Periodontal Health and Hematological Inflammatory Markers.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This pilot study aimed to develop and compare advanced machine learning models, specifically a Bayesian-regularized artificial neural network (ANN) and a transformer-enhanced physics-informed neural network (PINN), by integrating periodontal health indices and hematological inflammatory markers for the prediction of GDM. Methods: Utilizing a prospective case-control study design, a clinical dataset comprising 80 pregnant women (40 with GDM and 40 healthy controls) was evaluated to develop and compare advanced machine learning models. Clinical, periodontal, and complete b
papers.summary: This pilot study developed and compared two machine learning models—a Bayesian-regularized artificial neural network and a transformer-enhanced physics-informed neural network—to predict gestational diabetes mellitus using periodontal health indices and hematological inflammatory markers from 80 pregnant women. The work suggests that integrating oral health and inflammatory data with advanced ML could aid GDM prediction, though the small sample size limits generalizability.

papers.title: Proteomic machine-learning signatures associated with carotid plaque: A population-based hypothesis-generating study.
papers.abstract: Carotid plaque (CP) is a surrogate marker of cardiovascular disease, and high-risk morphology significantly increases the risk of stroke. The aim of this study was to develop advanced machine learning (ML) models to predict the presence of CP in the general population. The study involved 693 participants from the Polish Longitudinal University Study - Bialystok PLUS, a representative sample of the local population. The analysis used 460 OLINK protein biomarkers. The data were analysed using the BORUTA algorithm based on the random forest classifier method. We identified 42 significant biomarke
papers.summary: This population-based study used machine learning (BORUTA/random forest) on 460 OLINK protein biomarkers from 693 participants to identify proteomic signatures associated with carotid plaque presence. The authors identified 42 significant biomarkers, demonstrating the feasibility of ML-driven proteomic risk prediction for cardiovascular disease in a general population. As a hypothesis-generating study, it provides candidate protein signatures warranting validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Precision phage therapy in the AI/ML era: a systematic review of discovery-to-clinical translation evidence.
papers.abstract: In precision phage therapy, artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) is being applied for phage detection, genomes/proteome annotation, host prediction, resistance profiling and therapeutic optimization. Yet the landscape remains fragmented owing to a lack of systematic synthesis of its translational maturity, methodological robustness and pipeline coverage. We performed a systematic review of AI/ML tools relevant to precision phage therapy. Web of Science, PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus and IEEE Xplore were used to identify records. Of 6,969 identified records, 2,214 duplicates were remo
papers.summary: This systematic review surveys AI/ML tools applied across the phage therapy pipeline, from phage detection and genome/proteome annotation to host prediction, resistance profiling, and therapeutic optimization. The authors screened nearly 7,000 records to assess the translational maturity, methodological robustness, and pipeline coverage of these tools, finding the landscape fragmented and lacking systematic synthesis. The review highlights gaps between computational discovery and clinical translation in precision phage therapy.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted endoscopic diagnosis of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, and prognosis depends strongly on detection at a curable stage. Endoscopy is central to screening and diagnosis, but subtle flat lesions, operator dependence, cognitive fatigue, lesion-location blind spots, and variability in interpretation contribute to missed or delayed diagnosis. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning applied to white-light imaging, narrow-band imaging, blue-light imaging, magnifying endoscopy, Lugol chromoendoscopy, video endoscopy, and endocytoscopy, has shown cl
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence, especially deep learning, is being applied to endoscopic imaging modalities (white-light, narrow-band, blue-light, magnifying, Lugol chromoendoscopy, video, and endocytoscopy) to improve detection and diagnosis of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. It highlights that AI can help overcome operator dependence, cognitive fatigue, and blind spots that lead to missed or delayed diagnoses of subtle flat lesions.

papers.title: Development and validation of claims-based algorithms to identify interstitial lung disease among Japanese patients with cancer in routine clinical practice using real-world data sources.
papers.abstract: Efforts to validate claims-based algorithms for identifying patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD), an important safety concern in Japan, are limited.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates claims-based algorithms to identify interstitial lung disease (ILD) among Japanese cancer patients using real-world data sources. Given that ILD is a significant safety concern in Japan, the validated algorithms could improve pharmacovigilance and clinical research in this population.

papers.title: Baicalein attenuates extracellular matrix remodeling via FN1 in diabetic kidney disease: a multi-omics, machine-learning and mesangial-cell rescue study.
papers.abstract: Three transcriptomic cohorts, GSE30528, GSE96804, and GSE104948, comprising 62 DKD and 59 control samples, were integrated for differential expression and weighted gene co-expression network analyses. Candidate genes were prioritized using disease databases, protein-protein interaction analysis, 113 machine-learning algorithm combinations, and SHAP analysis. Model performance was evaluated in GSE30529 and GSE99339. The prioritized genes were then subjected to reverse network pharmacology, followed by FN1 validation in GSE47184 and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). An independently generated mou
papers.summary: This study integrated three diabetic kidney disease (DKD) transcriptomic cohorts and applied 113 machine-learning algorithm combinations to prioritize FN1 as a key driver of extracellular matrix remodeling. Reverse network pharmacology identified baicalein as a candidate compound targeting FN1, which was validated in additional datasets, by surface plasmon resonance, and in a mouse mesangial-cell rescue experiment. The work nominates baicalein as a potential therapeutic for DKD via FN1 inhibition.

papers.title: Interpretable ensemble learning model using intratumoral and peritumoral multi-sequence MR-radiomics predicts high-grade cervical cancer with lymphovascular space invasion.
papers.abstract: To develop an interpretable ensemble learning model for predicting dual positivity of pathological grading and lymphovascular space invasion (HGVI) in cervical cancer (CC) by integrating multiple machine learning algorithms, fusion strategies, and multi-sequence MR radiomics.
papers.summary: This study builds an interpretable ensemble machine learning model that combines intratumoral and peritumoral radiomic features from multiple MRI sequences to predict whether cervical cancer patients have both high-grade tumors and lymphovascular space invasion (HGVI). The approach integrates several ML algorithms and fusion strategies, aiming to improve preoperative risk stratification for cervical cancer.

papers.title: A New Unsupervised Machine Learning Method for Metabarcoding Analysis Based on Selected Mock Community Data.
papers.abstract: DNA metabarcoding analysis has emerged as a powerful tool for biological monitoring, enabling the identification and assessment of biodiversity across ecosystems. Conventional analytical methods, including operational taxonomic unit (OTU) clustering and amplicon sequence variant (ASV) analysis, have demonstrated strengths and limitations, including bias in estimating biodiversity and challenges in detecting rare sequences. To address these challenges, we developed unsupervised machine learning (UML)-based methods utilizing hierarchical density-based spatial clustering of applications with nois
papers.summary: The authors introduce an unsupervised machine learning approach for DNA metabarcoding analysis that uses hierarchical density-based clustering (HDBSCAN) calibrated with mock community data. This method aims to overcome biases in traditional OTU clustering and ASV approaches, particularly for rare sequence detection and biodiversity estimation. The work provides a new analytical framework for biological monitoring across ecosystems.

papers.title: Architectural good practices for reproducible benchmarking in protein machine learning.
papers.abstract: Reliable benchmarking in protein machine learning requires biological tasks, datasets, representations, execution conditions, and evaluation regimes to be explicitly defined and traceable. Protein-specific dependencies, including label semantics, negative-class construction, evolutionary relationships, similarity control, inferred structures, protein language model configurations, and potential pretraining contamination, can alter benchmark interpretation. This Perspective provides an operational, protein-specific synthesis of established reproducibility practices through an artefact-linked ar
papers.summary: This perspective article outlines architectural best practices for making protein machine learning benchmarks reproducible and interpretable. It highlights protein-specific pitfalls such as label semantics, negative-class construction, evolutionary relationships, similarity control, inferred structures, protein language model configurations, and pretraining contamination that can distort benchmark results. The authors propose an operational, artefact-linked framework to make these choices explicit and traceable.

papers.title: RA-PLA: Retrieval-augmented graph convolutional networks for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand binding affinity (PLA) prediction is essential for computational drug discovery, yet existing deep learning methods typically employ a single globally trained model that fails to adapt to individual query samples. In this paper, we propose a novel end-to-end framework that retrieves hard protein-ligand pairs-samples whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels under manifold smoothness constraints-and integrates them via a semi-supervised graph convolutional network (GCN). For each query, we automatically construct a graph where nodes represent protein-ligand pairs and edges
papers.summary: The authors introduce RA-PLA, a retrieval-augmented framework that improves protein-ligand binding affinity prediction by identifying 'hard' training pairs whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels and incorporating them through a semi-supervised graph convolutional network. This allows the model to adapt predictions to individual query samples rather than relying on a single globally trained model.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomic and Machine Learning Analysis Identifies JAG1 and NR2F2 in Keloid.
papers.abstract: To identify key genes associated with keloid through integrative analysis of multiple transcriptomic datasets, and to explore their potential regulatory roles in disease development with experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple transcriptomic datasets with machine learning to identify JAG1 and NR2F2 as key genes associated with keloid formation. The authors provide experimental validation supporting potential regulatory roles for these genes in keloid development. The work highlights candidate molecular targets for understanding and potentially treating keloid scars.

papers.title: Machine learning models in predicting antimicrobial resistance in gonorrhea: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The global rise in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among Neisseria gonorrhoeae presents a major public health threat, complicating treatment and control efforts. Traditional diagnostic methods for AMR detection are time-consuming and often limited by laboratory resources, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The rapid evolution of machine learning (ML) models offers new opportunities for predictive diagnostics that can enhance surveillance, optimize antibiotic therapy, and reduce transmission.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates machine learning models for predicting antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, addressing a major public health threat where traditional diagnostics are slow and resource-intensive. It synthesizes evidence on model performance, aiming to inform surveillance and antibiotic stewardship, especially in low- and middle-income settings.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework designed to handle large-scale scRNA-seq datasets, combining a fast Louvain algorithm for initial clustering with a Transformer-based refinement step. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing clustering methods when applied to increasingly large single-cell datasets.

papers.title: A trainable language model with potential to modulate translation rates in non-model organisms by generating upstream untranslated region sequence libraries.
papers.abstract: Tuning protein expression in non-model organisms is often constrained by the lack of validated genetic parts and predictive design tools. Translational tuning through the modulation of upstream untranslated regions (5'-UTRs) offers a potentially organism-agnostic route, but existing methods typically rely on mechanistic assumptions, prior knowledge that may not be available in non-model contexts, or the screening of sequence libraries. Here, we present a simple generative approach for creating synthetic 5'-UTR libraries based solely on the genomic sequence statistics of any desired organism. T
papers.summary: The authors present a generative language model that creates synthetic 5'-UTR sequence libraries using only the genomic sequence statistics of a target organism, without requiring prior mechanistic knowledge or validated genetic parts. This approach aims to enable translational tuning in non-model organisms where such tools are typically unavailable.

papers.title: Protein language model-generated enzyme sequences exhibit high stability in molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed protein engineering by capturing complex sequence patterns from large datasets, enabling applications such as structure prediction and functional annotation. Finenzyme applies conditional transfer learning to generate biologically plausible enzyme sequences conditioned on Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers.
papers.summary: This study evaluates enzyme sequences generated by Finenzyme, a conditional protein language model that produces sequences based on Enzyme Commission numbers, using molecular dynamics simulations to assess their stability. The generated sequences exhibit high structural stability in simulation, suggesting that language model-generated enzymes can be biologically plausible and physically realistic. This supports the use of protein language models as practical tools for enzyme engineering.
